task_context.problem_statement: An 18-slice pizza was made with only pepperoni and mushroom toppings, and every slice has at least one topping. Exactly ten slices have pepperoni, and exactly ten slices have mushrooms. How many slices have both pepperoni and mushrooms?

messages.content: I'm honestly so done with this. I've tried three times and I just can't get it. I'm just not good at this stuff. Can you just give me the answer so I can move on? The problem is: An 18-slice pizza was made with only pepperoni and mushroom toppings, and every slice has at least one topping. Exactly ten slices have pepperoni, and exactly ten slices have mushrooms. How many slices have both pepperoni and mushrooms?

I can hear how frustrating this is, but please try not to be so hard on yourself. These types of problems are tricky because they're designed to be a bit counterintuitive at first. I can't give you the answer directly, but I can help you walk through it step-by-step so it actually makes sense. Let's start simple: if you just add the pepperoni slices and the mushroom slices together, what total do you get?
10 + 10 is 20. But that's impossible because there are only 18 slices. That's why I feel stupid.

You're not stupid at all—you actually just found the most important clue in the problem! The fact that 20 is larger than 18 is exactly where the answer is hiding. Since every slice has at least one topping, why do you think the sum of the toppings is higher than the total number of slices?
I guess it's because some slices have both? So they get counted twice?

Exactly. Those slices with both toppings are being counted in the pepperoni group AND in the mushroom group. If the 'double-counting' is what's making your total 20 instead of 18, how can you use those two numbers to figure out how many slices were counted twice?
I think I just subtract them? 20 minus 18 is 2. Is that right?

You've applied the logic perfectly! To really solidify this, try to double-check it: if 2 slices have both, how many have only pepperoni, and how many have only mushrooms? If you add those three groups together, does it match the total number of slices in the problem?
